core_obligations: Set up the functors (proof lines 6410-6420): the assumptions give that f^* is exact and preserves the subcategories, so it passes to a functor between the derived categories, with Rf_* in the other direction by assumption (3).

Show the adjunction is an equivalence (proof lines 6420-6431): the unit and counit are isomorphisms on the subcategories by assumption (3) and its counterpart, so the two functors are quasi-inverse equivalences.
proof_roadmap: Pass f^* to the derived categories using exactness and preservation of the subcategories.
Use assumption (3) to identify the composites with the identities on the subcategories.
Conclude the equivalence with quasi-inverse Rf_*.
difficulty_reason: The lemma upgrades an equivalence of weak Serre subcategories of modules to an equivalence of their bounded below derived categories, for a flat morphism of ringed topoi (statement lines 6390-6408). The proof passes the pullback to the derived categories using exactness and the preservation of the subcategories (proof lines 6410-6420), and then uses the unit and counit identifications to conclude that the two functors are quasi-inverse (proof lines 6420-6431). The non-formal content is the passage from an equivalence of abelian subcategories to one of their derived categories. The claim is H2: a short categorical argument, written out.
